Questions¶

Q1. Marks Matrix

In [ ]:
import numpy as np

# Store the marks in a NumPy array
marks = np.array([
    [80, 70, 90, 60],
    [75, 85, 95, 65],
    [60, 70, 80, 90]
])

# Print the marks of the 2nd student (index 1)
print("Marks of 2nd student:", marks[1])

# Print all marks of subject 3 (index 2)
print("Marks of subject 3:", marks[:, 2])

# Print the highest mark
print("Highest mark:", marks.max())

Marks of 2nd student: [75 85 95 65]
Marks of subject 3: [90 95 80]
Highest mark: 95

Q2. Slice Without Loop

In [ ]:
import numpy as np

arr = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70])

# Extract values at even positions
even_positioned = arr[::2]

print(even_positioned)

[10 30 50 70]

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = np.array([80, 85, 90, 95, 100, 105, 110, 115, 120, 125])
y = np.array([240, 250, 260, 270, 280, 290, 300, 310, 320, 330])

font1 = {'family':'serif','color':'blue','size':20}
font2 = {'family':'serif','color':'darkred','size':15}

In [ ]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

x = np.array([1,2,3,4])
temp = np.array([22, 24, 19, 23])
sales = np.array([200, 300, 250, 400])

plt.figure(figsize=(5,10))

plt.subplot(2, 1, 1)
plt.plot(x, temp)
plt.title("Temperature")

plt.subplot(2, 1, 2)
plt.plot(x, sales)
plt.title("Sales")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Questions¶

Q3. Temperature Plot

In [ ]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Daily temperatures
temperatures = [22, 24, 19, 23, 25, 21, 20]

# Day numbers
days = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]

# Plotting
plt.plot(days, temperatures, marker='o')

# Labels and title
plt.xlabel("Day number")
plt.ylabel("Temperature")
plt.title("Weekly Temperature")

# Display the plot
plt.show()

Q4. Compare two Students

In [ ]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Marks of students
A = [70, 75, 80, 85]
B = [60, 65, 78, 88]

# Subject numbers (X-axis)
subjects = [1, 2, 3, 4]

# Plotting both students
plt.plot(subjects, A, marker='o', label='Student A')
plt.plot(subjects, B, marker='o', label='Student B')

# Labels and title
plt.xlabel("Subjects")
plt.ylabel("Marks")
plt.title("Performance Comparison of Two Students")

# Legend
plt.legend()

# Show plot
plt.show()

Q5. Debug the Graph

In [ ]:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4])
y = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40])

plt.plot(x, y)
plt.xlabel("X values")
plt.ylabel("Y values")
plt.title("Corrected Graph")
plt.show()

Q6. Kinematics

In [ ]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Given data
speed = [10, 20, 30, 40]
time = [1, 2, 3, 4]
distance = [10, 40, 90, 160]

# Create subplots (2 rows, 1 column)
plt.subplot(2, 1, 1)
plt.plot(time, speed, marker='o')
plt.xlabel("Time")
plt.ylabel("Speed")
plt.title("Speed vs Time")

plt.subplot(2, 1, 2)
plt.plot(time, distance, marker='o')
plt.xlabel("Time")
plt.ylabel("Distance")
plt.title("Distance vs Time")

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Show the plots
plt.show()

Data Cleaning means fixing or removing incorrect, incomplete, or duplicate data.

Bad data includes:

  • Empty cells (NaN values)
  • Wrong data formats
  • Incorrect values
  • Duplicate rows
In [ ]:
